about: What each agent host gives Coordn8, per mechanism, and how sure we are. 'confirmed' = read in the host's own public documentation on the date given, at the URL given. 'assumed' = believed but NOT checked against that host's documentation (this build was only allowed to consult Anthropic's public docs), so Coordn8 must work without it and every assumed row names the fallback. 'unsupported' = the way Coordn8 is delivered to that host gives the mechanism no way in (for example a pasted prompt has no hook configuration). Read by scripts/host_detect.py and scripts/federation.py; rendered for people in docs/HOST_INTEGRATION.md. A menu, never a fence: an invented mechanism a host offers may be used when it is recorded here with its evidence.

local-adapters.url: build/generate_adapters.py + scripts/install/installer.py (this package; not the host's documentation)

not-checked.url: not checked: this build may consult only Anthropic public docs; basis is how this package installs itself for the host

detection.about: How scripts/host_detect.py recognises the host, strongest first. It reads environment variables and files in the working directory up to the nearest git root; it never uses the network. COORDN8_HOST overrides everything.

env_signals.note: Set to 1 in subprocesses Claude Code spawns (Bash tool, hooks, stdio MCP servers). IDE extensions also set it in their integrated terminals, so it can appear in a terminal where the user, not the agent, is typing.
Present when the process was spawned directly by a tool call or hook.

detection.env_signals_not_recorded: No environment variable is recorded for codex, cursor or kiro: none was checked against those hosts' documentation, so detection there uses project files or COORDN8_HOST.

file_signals.note: AGENTS.md is read by several tools, so it is the weakest file signal.
A project .claude/ folder says the project is set up for Claude Code, not that Claude Code is running now.

federation.about: How scripts/federation.py matches installed skills to Coordn8's stages. Each phrase is matched as a whole word (an optional plural s/es is allowed) in the skill's name, description and when_to_use; a hit in the name counts double. A skill is a candidate for a stage when its score reaches min_score. A candidate is only a suggestion: it is used when a probe shows its output passes that stage's gates. Coordn8 stays complete when nothing matches: every stage has a built-in implementation.

connector_stages.about: Keyword (matched in an MCP server name or a tool name, case-insensitive) -> the stages that tool may serve. Suggestions only: no stage ever requires a connector or an MCP server.
connector_stages.claude_ai_tool_prefix_note: The docs say connectors appear in /mcp marked as coming from claude.ai; the exact tool-name prefix was not found in the docs on the date checked, so this prefix is an assumption. A connector is also recognised when a server name in the session's MCP list (for example the mcp_servers array of a headless system/init event) starts with claude_server_prefix, which is equally an assumption.
